meta.title: Astrolabe B — Thirty-Six Monthly Entries
meta.description: The monthly list of Astrolabe B (KAV 218 / VAT 9416), organized as twelve months with one name in each of the Ea, Anu and Enlil paths. This is a comparison for investigating Mazzaroth; their identity is not established.
meta.methodology: The calendar follows the names and path assignments in Astrolabe B. Modern positions come from catalogue reference stars or the spherical centres of selected star groups. Eleven entries have no assigned catalogue position. Dilbat, Šulpae, Salbatanu and Marduk have later planetary associations; their referents in this list are disputed.
meta.notes: Cifola and Hughey (2023) interpret the monthly triads as seasonal reminders within a religious narrative. A connection with the Median Magi is unconfirmed. Month numbers indicate calendar assignments. Ring order follows preserved circular astrolabes: Enlil inside, Anu middle, Ea outside (Monroe 2022); the diagram uses equal sectors and schematic ring spacing.
meta.coordinateLabel: ICRS · epoch 2000 where proper motion is available
meta.properMotionNote: pmRaMasYr is mu_alpha*cos(delta), and pmDecMasYr is mu_delta, both in milliarcseconds per Julian year. Native position and epoch are retained where available. Missing motion is not replaced by an invented measurement. A linear tangent-vector propagation omits radial-velocity perspective acceleration, orbital motion, and catalogue covariance; ancient extrapolations remain approximate. Group locators require propagation of their individual anchors followed by a new spherical centroid.
meta.catalogueSummary: 12,200 Gaia DR2 records retrieved (G ≤ 6.5). The displayed background contains 9,485 Gaia DR2 and 3,010 Hipparcos records (V ≤ 6.5), after suppressing 2,715 Gaia display points within 3 arcseconds of a Hipparcos fallback marker. This display-overlap rule does not establish a new physical crossmatch. BSC5 supplies cross-identifications and a resolver fallback. Gaia positions at J2015.5 and Hipparcos positions at J1991.25 have been propagated to J2000 with linear proper motions. Original values and reference epochs are retained. Objects without proper motion retain their native epoch. This is not precession to an ancient epoch; annual parallax and perspective acceleration are not modeled. Background is selected at Gaia G≤6.5, supplemented with unmatched Hipparcos Johnson V≤6.5. G and V are different passbands; marker sizes are illustrative, not calibrated visible-light photometry. No additional astrometric-quality cut is applied; an archive match is not validation of an ancient identification.

catalogueProvenance.epochNote: Gaia positions at J2015.5 and Hipparcos positions at J1991.25 have been propagated to J2000 with linear proper motions. Original values and reference epochs are retained. Objects without proper motion retain their native epoch. This is not precession to an ancient epoch; annual parallax and perspective acceleration are not modeled.
catalogueProvenance.photometryNote: Background is selected at Gaia G≤6.5, supplemented with unmatched Hipparcos Johnson V≤6.5. G and V are different passbands; marker sizes are illustrative, not calibrated visible-light photometry.
catalogueProvenance.displayDeduplicationNote: Gaia display points within 3 arcsec of a bright Hipparcos fallback are suppressed to avoid overlapping markers. This display-only positional coalescence does not assign Gaia IDs to HIP sources or establish new physical crossmatches. All raw Gaia rows and the pair audit are retained.
catalogueProvenance.qualityNote: The Gaia subset uses a G-magnitude cut only: no astrometric or photometric quality filter. DR2 is incomplete at the bright end, and individual bright-source magnitudes or solutions can be problematic. Gaia source IDs are retained as strings. The 155 Gaia sources without proper motion retain their native J2015.5 coordinate epoch.

queries.gaiaADQL:
SELECT g.source_id,g.ra,g.dec,g.ref_epoch,g.pmra,g.pmdec,g.parallax,g.phot_g_mean_mag,g.bp_rp,h.original_ext_source_id AS hip
FROM gaiadr2.gaia_source AS g
LEFT OUTER JOIN gaiadr2.hipparcos2_best_neighbour AS h ON g.source_id=h.source_id
WHERE g.phot_g_mean_mag <= 6.5

poleCalibration.summary: Polaris lies 0.7359° (44.1534 arcminutes) from the fixed ICRS north pole at stellar epoch 2000. It is close to the center, not coincident with it.
poleCalibration.projection: The plot is defined around the ICRS north pole. Its radius is proportional to 90° minus declination. That coordinate choice does not independently identify the center of an ancient diagram.
poleCalibration.orientation: At zero rotation: 0h RA is up, 6h right, 12h down, 18h left. RA increases clockwise. A star’s plotted angle equals its RA in degrees plus the rotation setting; this is a stated chart orientation, not a local compass bearing.
poleCalibration.epochNote: Stellar positions are propagated to epoch 2000 where proper motion is available. No ancient precession is applied. The current apparent celestial pole and its historical positions require date-dependent Earth-orientation and precession models.
